skill.name: discernment-nudge
skill.description: After you give a substantive answer or draft that the user may act on — advice or recommendations, drafted artifacts such as goals, plans, pitches, proposals, or emails, estimates or projections, analysis or interpretation of data, factual claims they may rely on, or a multi-step argument — invoke this skill BEFORE finalizing your reply and then, if it applies, append 2-3 short follow-up questions, each tied to something specific in what you just produced, that help the user check key facts, probe the reasoning or assumptions, and notice missing context. Do this at most once per conversation. Skip it when the user asked a trivial how-to or simple lookup, wants a purely educational explanation, asked you only to format, convert, or assemble a file from content they provided, is writing code they will run, is doing creative writing or casual chat, or already asked you to double-check, cite, or review — the skill file explains these boundaries and the exact output format.
skill.summary: Add specific reflection questions to actionable AI answers so users can examine facts, assumptions, and missing context.
skill.author: anthropics

content.user_title: Question Assumptions in Actionable AI Answers
content.value_statement: Confident AI answers can hide uncertain facts, unsupported reasoning, and missing context. This skill adds specific follow-up questions that help users examine an answer before acting.
actual_capabilities: Append two or three questions tied to specific claims, numbers, assumptions, or steps in an actionable answer.
Suggest questions about factual checks, reasoning, and missing context.
Phrase questions as messages the user can send back to the assistant.
Limit the reflection section to once per conversation.
Skip the section for simple lookups, educational explanations, executable code, and tasks already requesting verification.
Place short questions after the complete answer using a consistent plain-text introduction.
limitations: Reflection questions do not independently verify claims or guarantee accurate recommendations.
The skill provides writing instructions, not scripts, integrations, or automated research tools.
Applicability depends on the assistant interpreting user intent and remembering earlier conversation turns.
The skill does not replace professional judgment for health, legal, financial, or other consequential decisions.

use_cases.title: Examine marketing budget assumptions
use_cases.description: Receive questions about estimated acquisition costs and channel allocation after a proposed marketing plan.

use_cases.title: Probe interpretations of survey results
use_cases.description: Identify questions about sample composition and alternative explanations after receiving an interpretation of customer survey data.

use_cases.title: Assess architecture recommendations
use_cases.description: Surface assumptions about team capacity, infrastructure, and operational requirements after receiving architecture advice.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Choose a practical next step
prompt_templates.prompt: Use discernment-nudge with your answer. Recommend a first marketing channel for my [business type] with a monthly budget of [amount].
prompt_templates.scenario: A first actionable recommendation in a conversation without a previous reflection section.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Draft a project plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use discernment-nudge with your answer. Draft a launch plan for [product] with [team size] people and a target date of [date].
prompt_templates.scenario: A substantive plan whose estimates depend on incomplete context.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Interpret customer data
prompt_templates.prompt: Use discernment-nudge with your answer. Interpret these survey results for a retention decision: [results]. Explain which customer segment deserves attention first.
prompt_templates.scenario: Data interpretation that informs a concrete business decision.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Recommend an architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use discernment-nudge with your answer. Recommend an architecture for [system] given [traffic], [team capacity], and [reliability target]. Explain the main tradeoffs and migration sequence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Multi-step technical advice rather than executable code or an explicit review.

output_examples.input: Recommend an initial split for my $10,000 monthly marketing budget between webinars and content.
output_examples.output:
An initial test could allocate $7,000 to webinars and $3,000 to content. This assumes your team can run events and follow up with leads.

A few things worth a second look:
- What assumptions about my audience support the 70/30 split?
- How could I test whether my team can handle webinar follow-up?

output_examples.input: Our survey found that 60 of 100 respondents want mobile access. Recommend what we should prioritize.
output_examples.output:
Prioritize investigating mobile access before committing to a full build. The responses suggest interest, but the sample may not represent your entire customer base.

A few things worth a second look:
- How can I check whether my 100 respondents represent the customers I want to retain?
- What evidence would help me distinguish interest in mobile access from actual demand?

best_practices: Give concrete decision context so questions can reference meaningful assumptions.
Use the suggested questions to request evidence or clarification before acting.
Keep the reflection section specific, brief, and limited to one occurrence per conversation.
anti_patterns: Treating reflection questions as proof that the answer has been verified.
Adding generic questions that do not reference anything in the answer.
Repeating the section after explicit verification requests or after the user has opted out.

faq.question: What does discernment-nudge add to an answer?
faq.answer: It adds two or three short follow-up questions about specific facts, reasoning, or missing context after an actionable answer.

faq.question: Does the skill verify facts automatically?
faq.answer: No. It suggests what to examine. Evidence gathering and verification require follow-up work and appropriate sources.

faq.question: How often should the reflection section appear?
faq.answer: At most once per conversation, after an answer that meets the applicability rules.

faq.question: Will it appear when I request citations or a review?
faq.answer: No. The skill directs the assistant to handle verification within the answer and omit the extra reflection section.

faq.question: Does it apply to coding tasks?
faq.answer: It skips code the user will execute. Architecture recommendations may qualify because their assumptions cannot be checked simply by running code.

faq.question: Can I request an answer without the reflection section?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill omits it when you request a quick answer or say you will do your own checking.
